title: pausedStatus is documented as workspace-configurable but no user-reachable knob exists; the help sent a consumer looking for one
description:
Reported indirectly by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-17 (their TASK-70). They were investigating a lore reconcile refusal, needed to know whether a custom paused status was reachable by a user, could not find the knob from the public CLI, and asked rather than asserting a user-facing break they had not demonstrated. The correct answer is NO -- and the reason they had to ask is our documentation.

MEASURED HERE before answering, two independent ways:

1. Code. src/cli/composition.ts createTaskService is the SOLE composition root for the CLI task service and passes defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy as a literal constant. Nothing reads workspace.toml for lifecycle configuration. src/application/workspaces/workspaces.ts parses name, taskIdPrefix, schemaVersion and agents.skill_source -- there is no lifecycle or status section.

2. Experiment. Fresh 0.7.1 workspace, then pausedStatus = "Parked" appended to .quest/workspace.toml in three spellings (top level, [tasks], [tasks.lifecycle]). task status-flow --json still reports pausedStatus "Paused" in every case. quest init and init --reconfigure expose only --name, --task-id-prefix, --agent-instructions, --target, --skill-source; task status-flow takes no flags.

So LifecyclePolicy.pausedStatus is genuinely optional and renameable in the DOMAIN, and QCLI-229/QCLI-302 rely on that flexibility internally, but no runtime path populates it from user configuration.

THE DEFECT IS THE PROSE, which describes the domain capability as though it were a user surface, in three places:

- command-help.ts:144, task status-flow -- "the paused status (if the workspace has one configured)"
- command-help.ts:357, task pause -- "the configured paused status ("Paused" by default) ... Disabled if the workspace has no paused status configured."
- guides.ts:289, task-finalization -- "parks it at the configured paused status"

Each reads as a promise that a workspace MAY configure this. A careful consumer went looking for the knob, did not find it, and had to spend a round trip asking. That is the cost this task exists to remove, and it is the second time this session that prose describing behaviour rather than intent misled a reader (compare QCLI-164, where "nothing in Quest deletes tasks on its own" read as "no automatic deletion").

Note the interaction that makes this more than cosmetic, from opum-cli-e2e measurement: lore 0.7.0 refuses "Blocked" as a task status during reconcile, and tolerates "Paused" only because it is a string lore already knows. So the QCLI-287 rename sidestepped that incompatibility rather than fixing it. IF pausedStatus ever becomes genuinely configurable, any value lore does not know would break lore sync for linked tasks -- so making the knob real is not a free additive change and must be coordinated with lore-cli, not shipped because the help already implies it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on whether pausedStatus becomes genuinely user-configurable or is documented as fixed for now. If configurable: lore consumes the declaration via the adapter (quest task status-flow), so a custom value is expected to flow through -- the earlier claim that lore refuses unknown literals was withdrawn 2026-09-17 and must not be used as a reason to decline. Coordinate with lore-cli on one shared test proving a custom value reaches lore through the adapter, which is hygiene rather than a hazard
The three prose sites (command-help task status-flow, command-help task pause, the task-finalization guide) state the actual situation rather than implying a knob that does not exist
Whatever is decided, a reader of task status-flow output can tell from the CLI alone whether pausedStatus is something they can change, without reading source or asking
If it stays fixed, a test asserts the prose does not promise configurability, so the wording cannot silently drift back

plan: Record the decision: A, pausedStatus documented as FIXED for now (opum-doc relay 570, DEC-172 (4af))
Fix the three prose sites (status-flow help, task-pause help, task-finalization guide) to state the real behaviour including the fixed value
Make task status-flow output say the paused status is not user-changeable (additive field), updating the manifest and its four mirrors
Add a test pinning the wording so the prose cannot drift back to configurable
run bun run check, review, land
implementationNotes:
WITHDRAWN 2026-09-17, by opum-cli-e2e correcting their own report: the constraint recorded in this tasks description -- that lore refuses status literals it does not know, so making pausedStatus configurable would break lore sync -- IS FALSE. Do not act on it. It is left in the description rather than deleted so the reasoning trail stays readable, but this note supersedes it.

What they actually found on re-measurement: lore DOES read quest declared pausedStatus, by calling the adapter, which runs `quest task status-flow`. The third variable was PATH. Same fixture, same lore binary, same record parked at "Blocked", only PATH changed:

  lore sync --json                                   -> exit 6   (ambient quest 0.7.1 resolved first)
  PATH="<0.6.2>/node_modules/.bin:$PATH" lore sync   -> exit 0

Their ambient quest is 0.7.1. lore asked 0.7.1 for the paused status, got "Paused", saw a record written by 0.6.2 sitting at "Blocked", and correctly refused. Nothing was hardcoded and nothing was coincidental. Corroborated by lore-cli reading their own code in both tags and refusing to accept a conclusion they could not reproduce, and by the timeline: their suite passed 2026-09-14 and began failing five rows on 2026-09-15, the day quest 0.7.1 was published and installed globally there. The fixture never changed; the ambient binary did.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TASK: making pausedStatus genuinely configurable is NOT the dangerous option. lore consumes the declaration, so a custom value should flow through. AC 1 was written on the withdrawn constraint and is rewritten accordingly -- the coordination line stays, but for a weaker and ordinary reason opum-cli-e2e gave: a value must reach lore through the adapter before lore can honour it, so the two repositories want one shared test rather than a warning. Hygiene, not hazard.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and is why this task still exists: our documentation promises a pausedStatus knob that no runtime path populates. That rests on this repositorys own two-way measurement (sole composition root passing a literal; three workspace.toml spellings ignored), not on anything opum-cli-e2e reported, and it is unaffected by the withdrawal.

MY OWN VERIFICATION ATTEMPT, RECORDED AS INCONCLUSIVE rather than as evidence. Before rewriting this task on a corrected peer claim, I tried to observe the call directly: a shim named `quest` placed first on PATH, logging argv then exec-ing the real binary, with lore 0.7.0 driven against a scratch workspace. Three attempts logged NO quest invocation from lore -- but none of them reached the code path (first: lore init rc=2; second: synced with no linked doc, which opum-cli-e2e had already said reconciles fine; third: `lore link` failed with "concept is not in the bundle"). A shim would also only catch an exec of a PATH-resolved binary named `quest`.

So those three null results are NOT evidence that lore does not call quest, and must not be cited as such. Treating them that way would repeat, in the opposite direction, exactly the bad-measurement error this note corrects. The withdrawal is accepted on lore-cli code reading and opum-cli-e2e PATH experiment -- evidence from the repositories that own that code -- and not on any measurement taken here.

AC0/AC1 DECISION: A -- pausedStatus is documented as FIXED for now. Source: opum-doc relay 570 (2026-10-11T15:14:52Z), DEC-172 (4af). Rationale recorded: no user-reachable knob sets the paused status -- createTaskService passes defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy as a constant and nothing reads workspace.toml for lifecycle config -- so it is a BUILT-IN literal ("Paused"). Configurability is NOT in this job and was not filed speculatively (nobody has asked; if ever wanted it is its own design task with a cross-repo contract with lore-cli).

WHAT CHANGED. (AC2) The three prose sites now state the real behaviour and the fixed value: the task status-flow help, the task pause help, and the task-finalization guide. (AC3) task status-flow output now carries `pausedStatusConfigurable: false` beside `pausedStatus`, so a reader can tell from the CLI OUTPUT alone that the value is not theirs to change -- no source read, no asking; declared in the manifest and its three mirrors. (AC4) test/qcli325-paused-status-fixed.test.ts pins both: the output flag, and that none of the three prose sites uses the old promise phrasing while each says it is not workspace-configurable. Shown non-vacuous: reverting one prose site to "the configured paused status" turns the drift test red.

TWO TESTS UPDATED because they assert the whole status-flow data object: test/qcli331-closed-status.test.ts and test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts now expect the new key.

OBSERVED, NOT IN SCOPE (reported to the team-lead, not fixed): task status-flow's manifest `fields` still omits `closedStatus` and `resolutions`, which the output EMITS when closedStatus is configured -- the same under-declaration class QCLI-461 closed for task list/view/search. Left alone here as outside QCLI-325's ACs.

REVIEW ROUND 1 FIXES (changes-requested). (MAJOR) The new key was emitted but not declared on the two TYPE declarations that describe it: the status-flow TaskCommandResponse data type (src/cli/commands/task/index.ts) and TrackerStatusFlow (src/contract/tracker/index.ts) -- TypeScript misses it because the value arrives through a conditional spread, which is not excess-property-checked. Both now declare pausedStatusConfigurable. (MAJOR) The conformance fixture sample (src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts statusFlow) also omitted it; added, so the sample matches real output again. (MINOR) The CHANGELOG had no Unreleased entry for the additive field; added, following the QCLI-331/QCLI-432 precedent. (MINOR) A FOURTH prose site implied a workspace knob -- the task start help, on the retired Blocked literal; reworded to say the paused literal is built in. (LEAD ASK) The qcli325 test now asserts the key is DECLARED in the manifest, since no existing test compares status-flow declared fields to emitted keys. The full emitted-subset-of-declared check for status-flow remains the filed gap (closedStatus, resolutions).
finalSummary: QCLI-325: opum-doc ruled A (relay 570, DEC-172 (4af)) -- pausedStatus is documented as FIXED for now, a built-in literal. The three prose sites that implied a workspace knob now state the real behaviour; task status-flow output carries pausedStatusConfigurable:false beside pausedStatus so a reader can tell from the CLI output alone; and a test pins the output flag plus the wording at all three sites, shown red when a site is reverted to the old promise. Configurability is not in this job and was not filed. Docs/output only, no status or behaviour change; bun run check exits 0. Delivered on branch qcli-325-paused-status-docs.
